assumptions_named.entry: Backout: recoverable files and Db2 undone, RECOVERY(NONE) files kept
READ ... INTO LENGTH: in-out, truncation and LENGERR; a VSAM file's LENGTH need not equal its record length; LENGERR on READ UPDATE refused
Terminal RECEIVE (INTO / SET, LENGTH, MAXLENGTH, NOTRUNCATE; LENGERR, EOC on an LUTYPE2 terminal) and SEND CONTROL

Interval control on the det port: START (INTERVAL / TIME / AFTER / AT, TERMID, REQID, PROTECT, FROM, RTRANSID / RTERMID / QUEUE, CHANNEL), RETRIEVE (INTO / LENGTH, the data options, ENVDEFERR), CANCEL REQID, RUN TRANSID CHILD [CHANNEL], FETCH ANY / CHILD (NOSUSPEND, TIMEOUT or waiting), FREE CHILD, and DELAY as the wait that dispatches RUN children (#4950); the child schedule, TIME RESP2 and the order of out-of-range checks assumed; ties, a child's region-resource commands, RETRIEVE SET / WAIT refused

ASSIGN on the det port: STARTCODE (TD / S / SD / D), USERID (the default user), FACILITY / SCRNHT / SCRNWD (INVREQ RESP2 5 without a terminal) from facts the harness states; no data area written when ASSIGN raises INVREQ; OPID, NETNAME, TERMCODE, FCI, the other screen sizes, work-area lengths and the rest refused
assumptions_named.status: ASSUMED (REFUSED where the harness cannot decide)

assumptions_named.entry: SEND TEXT on the det port and the stub: TERMINAL accepted as the default output disposition (the principal facility; the event is that of SEND TEXT without it); ACCUM, PAGING, SET, REQID, HEADER, TRAILER, JUSTIFY / JUSFIRST / JUSLAST, the printer, partition and LDC options, MSR, FMHPARM, DEFAULT / ALTERNATE refused
assumptions_named.status: MATCHED (REFUSED where the region cannot decide)

assumptions_named.entry: READ GTEQ / GENERIC on a KSDS: the first record whose key (or its first KEYLENGTH bytes) equals RIDFLD's or, with GTEQ, is greater, in the browse's key order (D1); NOTFND RESP2 80; READ UPDATE holds the record found; RIDFLD not updated; #4771: on a file named at run time the full key is that file's (looked up then), and DELETE GENERIC deletes every record with the generic key (NOTFND RESP2 80 when none); DELETE INVREQ RESP2 21 (ESDS), 22 (generic on a non-KSDS), 25 / 42 (GENERIC KEYLENGTH not shorter than the key / below zero) and 26 (KEYLENGTH without GENERIC) on both runtimes (#5092, as READ's: X52); refused: a GENERIC KEYLENGTH of zero, a non-constant KEYLENGTH and a RIDFLD shorter than the key searched
assumptions_named.status: ASSUMED (REFUSED where IBM is silent or the layout decides)

assumptions_named.entry: RETURN TRANSID ... IMMEDIATE: the task of TRANSID attached at once with the COMMAREA, ahead of any terminal input and any START request, the terminal's next operator step left alone; its EIBAID is not stated by IBM (the crucible runner gives none and a case never reads it), its STARTCODE TD; INVREQ RESP2 1 (no terminal), INVREQ RESP2 2 (below the highest level), LENGERR RESP2 11 return to the program; LINK ... SYNCONRETURN accepted and ignored (IBM: "ignored if the link is local"); IMMEDIATE without TRANSID, and both INVREQs at once (no terminal below level 1), refused
assumptions_named.status: ASSUMED (the STARTCODE; REFUSED where IBM is silent)

assumptions_named.entry: DEFINE COUNTER (COUNTER / POOL / VALUE; none: the initial value zero; a counter that exists: INVREQ RESP2 202; a pool or counter name outside IBM's characters: INVREQ RESP2 403 / 404) and DELETE COUNTER (a counter that is not there: INVREQ RESP2 201; a pool outside IBM's characters: 403); GET COUNTER and QUERY COUNTER answer INVREQ RESP2 201 for a counter that is not there (GET COUNTER answered NOTFND before: IBM lists none) and 403 / 404 for a bad pool / name; MINIMUM / MAXIMUM / NOSUSPEND / DCOUNTER, a VALUE below zero and a counter name of blanks refused

INQUIRE URIMAP's browse (START / NEXT / END with URIMAP, PATH, TRANSACTION: END RESP2 2 past the last definition, ILLOGIC RESP2 1 for a START while one is open; the installed definitions and their order are stated by whoever runs the task; a short value is padded with blanks; the areas are left alone on any condition other than NORMAL) and WRITE OPERATOR (TEXT, plus TEXTLENGTH, ROUTECODES / NUMROUTES and EVENTUAL since #5859, the routes unobserved; recorded as a WRITE-OPERATOR event); the direct form INQUIRE URIMAP(name) (modelled since #4768, X34), every other URIMAP attribute, a NEXT / END with no browse, and a console text IBM reformats (DFHnnnn / DFHaannnn, or over 113 characters) refused

DOCUMENT CREATE (DOCTOKEN; none, TEXT / BINARY with LENGTH, or TEMPLATE: an empty document, the area's bytes unchanged, or the text the installed DOCTEMPLATE yields; LENGERR RESP2 1 for a negative LENGTH, NOTFND RESP2 3 for a template not installed) and DOCUMENT RETRIEVE (DOCTOKEN, INTO, LENGTH, MAXLENGTH, DATAONLY: at most MAXLENGTH bytes INTO, LENGTH the document's length, LENGERR RESP2 2 when truncated, NOTFND RESP2 1 for an unknown token, LENGERR RESP2 1 for a negative MAXLENGTH); the DOCTOKEN value, the installed templates' text, and the text a retrieved document's bytes are in are ours / stated by whoever runs the task; FROM, FROMDOC, SYMBOLLIST / LISTLENGTH / DELIMITER / UNESCAPED, DOCSIZE, HOSTCODEPAGE / CHARACTERSET, a RETRIEVE without DATAONLY or MAXLENGTH, a CREATE of TEXT / BINARY without LENGTH, a template with symbols or template commands, and DOCUMENT INSERT / SET / DELETE refused

INQUIRE URIMAP(name) with no browse option reads that definition among the installed ones the run states (X32's list: PATH and TRANSACTION as a browse NEXT returns them, NOTFND RESP2 3 when it is not installed, a browse in progress left where it was); INQUIRE PROGRAM STATUS answers ENABLED (CVDA 23), the DEFINE PROGRAM default, for every program the region defines, on NORMAL only; a case CSD defining a program STATUS(DISABLED) refused

The HTTP server is a stated fact (http_peers: scheme, host, port, CLIENT URIMAP and path, and the response to each request, matched by method, path and query in order); WEB OPEN by URIMAP or HOST / HOSTLENGTH / PORTNUMBER (80 / 443 when omitted) / SCHEME returns our 8-byte token (GGWSnnnn), LENGERR 21, INVREQ 40 / 138; WEB CONVERSE sends METHOD, PATH (the URIMAP's when omitted), QUERYSTRING, FROM with MEDIATYPE, recorded as a WEB-CONVERSE event, and returns INTO (at most MAXLENGTH, INTO's length when omitted; LENGERR 57 when longer), TOLENGTH, STATUSCODE, the reason phrase's bytes and MEDIATYPE (blank-padded to 56), with NOTOPEN 27, INVREQ 33 / 34 / 54 / 76, LENGERR 5 / 8 / 16 / 50 / 59; WEB CLOSE NOTOPEN 27; the exchange is in the program's characters (conversion options change nothing); refused: an unstated peer or response, two conditions at once, TRACE / OPTIONS, MAXLENGTH 0, no PATH on a HOST session, a blank MEDIATYPE with a body, a reason phrase longer than STATUSLEN, a length past its area, and every option zECS does not use

WEB PARSE URL is pure: URL / URLLENGTH are split into SCHEMENAME (upper case, blank-padded to its 16-byte area), HOST / HOSTLENGTH, PORTNUMBER (explicit, else 80 for HTTP and 443 for HTTPS), PATH / PATHLENGTH (with its leading slash) and QUERYSTRING / QUERYSTRLEN (without its question mark, still escaped); each length option is read as the area's size and set to the piece's length; INVREQ 28 (no scheme and ://, an empty scheme or host, a port that is not 1-5 digits or above 65535: ASSUMED) and INVREQ 65 (a percent not followed by two of 0-9 A-F); the areas are written on NORMAL only; an IPv6 host is written in brackets and returned without them (IBM, per the crucible's gt-web-parse-url); LENGERR RESP2 29 / 30 / 8 (host / path / query string longer than its length) with the areas and lengths left alone (ASSUMED); refused: a scheme other than HTTP / HTTPS, user-info, a fragment, an IPv6 host that is not [hex:colons] or [hex:colons]:port, an empty port or port 0, a lowercase hex digit in an escape, a URLLENGTH not above zero or past its area, a length past its area, a PATH or QUERYSTRING asked for when the URL has none, two conditions at once (INVREQ and LENGERR, or two pieces too long), HOSTTYPE

The task serves one inbound HTTP request that whoever runs it STATES (http_request: scheme, host, port, method, version, path, query, headers, media type and body; unstated, WEB SEND is refused); WEB SEND FROM / FROMLENGTH, DOCTOKEN or CONTAINER [CHANNEL] with ACTION(IMMEDIATE), ACTION(EVENTUAL) or no ACTION, MEDIATYPE, STATUSCODE (200 when omitted), STATUSTEXT / STATUSLEN (the whole area when STATUSLEN is omitted), SRVCONVERT / NOSRVCONVERT and, for a document, DOCSTATUS(DOCDELETE | NODOCDELETE) is recorded as a WEB-SEND event (status, reason phrase or none, media type or none, body, action) and compared; an IMMEDIATE response is recorded when sent, an EVENTUAL one (and an omitted ACTION, IBM's default for a send that is not chunked) is held and recorded once at the end of the task, after the task's other events, a second EVENTUAL send replacing the first (the whole response: ASSUMED); DOCDELETE deletes the document once its contents are saved (a later request for it is NOTFND 1), NODOCDELETE (the default) keeps it; INVREQ 11 (an action that is neither IMMEDIATE nor EVENTUAL), INVREQ 72 (204 / 205 / 304 with a body), INVREQ 143 (an invalid DOCSTATUS), NOTFND 1 (a DOCTOKEN that names no document: not created, deleted or wrongly named); for a container body CONTAINERERR 2 (no such container), CHANNELERR 2 (no such channel), INVREQ 145 (no CHANNEL and no current channel), INVREQ 150 (SRVCONVERT on a DATATYPE BIT container); the response is in the program's characters (conversion changes nothing); refused: no stated request, an empty container body, a BIT container sent without conversion, FROM, DOCTOKEN or CHUNKING together with CONTAINER, CHANNEL without CONTAINER, a second send after an IMMEDIATE one, an IMMEDIATE send after an EVENTUAL one, a task that ended in an abend with an EVENTUAL response held, a WEB WRITE HTTPHEADER after any send, DOCSTATUS on a FROM send, FROMLENGTH or STATUSLEN not above zero, a length past its area, a STATUSCODE outside 100-599, a blank or malformed MEDIATYPE, SRVCONVERT on a media type that is not text/* or application/json, two conditions at once, and CHUNKING, CHARACTERSET, CLNTCODEPAGE, HOSTCODEPAGE, CLOSESTATUS, LENGTH

#4972: EXTRACT WEB is IBM's synonym of WEB EXTRACT (one table, one runtime call, the same answers and refusals); EXTRACT TCPIP reads the connection the run STATES (tcpip: client / server IPv4 address, the names the DNS knows, the port, the SSL type): CLIENTADDR / CADDRLENGTH, CLIENTNAME / CNAMELENGTH, SERVERADDR / SADDRLENGTH, SERVERNAME / SNAMELENGTH written as bytes with each length option set to the real length (areas on NORMAL only), CLIENTADDRNU / SERVERADDRNU (the address as a signed fullword), CLNTIPFAMILY / SRVRIPFAMILY (IPV4, 300), PORTNUMNU, SSLTYPE (SSL 1030 / NOSSL 1031 / CLIENTAUTH 1032 / ATTLSAWARE 1205); an area given with its length option missing or not above zero LENGERR RESP2 1; a client name the DNS does not know length 0, the area left alone, NORMAL; refused: no connection stated, an address that is not IPv4 dotted decimal (IPv6, CLNTADDR6NU / SRVRADDR6NU), an address number past a signed fullword, a SERVERNAME the connection does not state, a name or address longer than its length (LENGERR RESP2 3 / 4 / 6 / 7), PORTNUMBER (the character form), AUTHENTICATE, TCPIPSERVICE, PRIVACY, MAXDATALEN, a length past its area, two conditions at once. #4940: WEB READ FORMFIELD / QUERYPARM read the stated body form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded) / query string as name=value pairs joined by '&' (split at the first '=', only %XX unescaped), the name matched without case (IBM), two pairs of the name refused, NAMELENGTH / VALUELENGTH not above zero LENGERR RESP2 1, no data INVREQ RESP2 13, no such name NOTFND RESP2 1, a value longer than VALUELENGTH cut with LENGERR RESP2 5 and VALUELENGTH its real length; WEB STARTBROWSE / READNEXT / ENDBROWSE of HTTPHEADER, FORMFIELD, QUERYPARM keep a browse per kind (ILLOGIC RESP2 10 / 5 for a second start, INVREQ RESP2 43 / 13 for no headers / data, INVREQ RESP2 4 READNEXT / ENDBROWSE before a start, ENDFILE with RESP2 0 at the end, LENGERR RESP2 1 for a length not above zero with the browse left where it was, LENGERR RESP2 4 / 5 for a FORMFIELD / QUERYPARM name / value that does not fit, cut, the same pair returned again, lengths the real ones), a start name matched exactly (case-only or duplicate matches refused), a start that raises a condition starts no browse (ASSUMED); refused: the code-page options, the client form (SESSTOKEN), HTTPHEADER truncation on READNEXT, a body that is not application/x-www-form-urlencoded, data with a pair lacking '=', an empty name or pair, ';', '+', a bad escape, an escaped name or a byte outside printable ASCII, a READNEXT after ENDFILE, a name and value both too long, two conditions at once. #4767: The task serves the one inbound HTTP request that whoever runs it STATES (http_request, as X37; unstated, each command is refused); WEB EXTRACT (server form) returns the stated scheme (CVDA HTTP 1096 / HTTPS 1029), host, HTTP method, HTTP version (the text the run states: ASSUMED), path, query string (none: length 0, area left alone: ASSUMED), the port and REQUESTTYPE HTTPYES, each length option read as the area's size and set to the piece's length, the areas written on NORMAL only; LENGERR RESP2 21 / 5 / 7 for a HOSTLENGTH / PATHLENGTH / VERSIONLEN not above zero; WEB RECEIVE INTO / LENGTH / MAXLENGTH / MEDIATYPE returns the stated body (cut at MAXLENGTH with LENGERR RESP2 57, LENGTH the bytes returned, LENGERR RESP2 16 for a MAXLENGTH not above zero, MEDIATYPE blank-padded to 56) with SRVCONVERT / NOSRVCONVERT changing nothing (program characters); WEB READ HTTPHEADER returns the value of the stated header of that exact name (INVREQ RESP2 43 no headers, NOTFND RESP2 1 no such header, LENGERR RESP2 1 VALUELENGTH not above zero); WEB WRITE HTTPHEADER adds a header to the response, recorded as WEB-HEADER and compared (a name written twice is two headers; LENGERR RESP2 35 / 55); refused: NOTRUNCATE, containers, every code-page option, SERVERCONV, BODYCHARSET, TYPE, the client forms (SESSTOKEN, REALM), HOSTTYPE, URIMAP, a LENGERR on a piece or value longer than its length, a METHODLENGTH / QUERYSTRLEN not above zero, a request with no body, a second RECEIVE other than one SRVCONVERT pass after NOSRVCONVERT, a header found only without case or stated twice, a header written after the response was sent, a name with a blank or colon, a length past its area, two conditions at once

MOVE CONTAINER (rename across channels, TOCHANNEL made when absent, an existing AS overwritten) and STARTBROWSE / GETNEXT / ENDBROWSE CONTAINER (the names of a channel's containers, in creation order, one token per browse) with IBM's RESP / RESP2: INVREQ 4, CHANNELERR 2, CONTAINERERR 10, END 2, TOKENERR 3; refused: a move onto itself or onto the other data type, a browse of a channel that changed, a browse with no channel, and the conditions no modelled state reaches (CHANNELERR 1 / 3, CONTAINERERR 18, INVREQ 30 / 31, ILLOGIC 1)

A doubleword counter has the limits DEFINE DCOUNTER gave it (MINIMUM zero and MAXIMUM a doubleword of X'FF' when omitted; VALUE zero; INVREQ RESP2 407 for MAXIMUM below MINIMUM, 406 for VALUE below MINIMUM or above MAXIMUM + 1); GET DCOUNTER at MAXIMUM + 1 is SUPPRESSED RESP2 101 and leaves the counter, or with WRAP returns MINIMUM and goes on from it; QUERY DCOUNTER returns VALUE / MINIMUM / MAXIMUM; DELETE DCOUNTER; an INCREMENT beyond MAXIMUM - MINIMUM or past MAXIMUM + 1, a counter past a doubleword, and the limits of a counter DEFINE COUNTER made are refused

FORMATTIME YYDDD / YYYYDDD / YYDDMM / YYYYDDMM (the date's parts in IBM's order, the day of the year three digits) and DAYCOUNT (1 January 1900 is day 1) / DAYOFMONTH / DAYOFWEEK (Sunday=0) / MONTHOFYEAR / YEAR / MILLISECONDS (binary integers, written by the receiving area's declared usage); DATE / DATEFORM / FULLDATE (the installation's DATFORM), DATESTRING / STRINGFORMAT / STRINGZONE (the zone) refused by name; DUMP TRANSACTION and the bare DUMP form refused by name (the outcome is the region's dump setup)

A USAGE POINTER item holds the handle of a block of task storage; GETMAIN SET(ptr) FLENGTH / LENGTH INITIMG(byte) acquires one (every byte the INITIMG value; LENGERR RESP2 1 for FLENGTH below 1 or LENGTH zero, the pointer then zero), FREEMAIN DATAPOINTER(ptr) releases it (INVREQ RESP2 1 for an address GETMAIN did not return: a null pointer, a record's address), WEB RECEIVE SET(ptr) LENGTH(area) [MAXLENGTH] puts the request body in a new block (MAXLENGTH optional: all of it; LENGERR RESP2 16 leaves the pointer as it was, RESP2 57 cuts the body and sets it), SET ADDRESS OF record TO pointer / TO ADDRESS OF record makes a LINKAGE 01 record's bytes the block's (a real alias), SET ADDRESS OF record TO ADDRESS OF item (a subordinate item or a WORKING-STORAGE record) makes the record a window onto that item's bytes (Storage.base), SET pointer TO ADDRESS OF record / item gives its handle (block plus offset); refused: a literal INITIMG, a GETMAIN without INITIMG that acquires storage (at run time, on the det port and the stub), SHARED, NOSUSPEND, FREEMAIN DATA, a length above 256 MiB (LENGTH above 65520), a second FREEMAIN of the same block, FREEMAIN of a WEB RECEIVE SET body, SET ADDRESS OF a freed / unknown pointer, ADDRESS OF a table element, a pointer table named without its subscripts, SET ADDRESS OF ... TO NULL, a pointer a REDEFINES overlays (pointer arithmetic)

READ NOTFND RESP2 80 and INVREQ 25 / 26 / 42 for a KEYLENGTH (#5092), READ UPDATE TOKEN(d) returns a fullword token for the record held; REWRITE / DELETE / UNLOCK TOKEN(t) act on that record, and a token that matches none in use (never issued, spent, another file's) is INVREQ RESP2 47; a SYNCPOINT ends every token. The token's value is ASSUMED (the task's 1, 2, 3, ...). Refused: READNEXT / READPREV UPDATE [TOKEN] (RLS only), DELETE TOKEN with RIDFLD or GENERIC, REWRITE TOKEN whose FROM has another key

REWIND resets a counter that has reached its limit (MAXIMUM + 1) to its minimum, else SUPPRESSED RESP2 102, INVREQ 406 for an INCREMENT beyond (maximum - minimum) + 1; UPDATE sets the current value (INVREQ 406 below MINIMUM or above MAXIMUM + 1); GET REDUCE leaves a counter an INCREMENT would carry past MAXIMUM + 1 at MAXIMUM + 1, GET COMPAREMIN / COMPAREMAX hand the value out only when it is in range (either bound when COMPAREMAX is below COMPAREMIN), else SUPPRESSED RESP2 103 and the counter stays; NOSUSPEND is accepted and changes nothing (one task, no coupling-facility structure, so BUSY RESP2 500 cannot occur). Refused: UPDATE COMPAREMIN / COMPAREMAX, REWIND INCREMENT above 1, REDUCE with WRAP or at a counter already at its limit, COMPARE at a counter already at its limit, a negative VALUE / compare value of a fullword counter, REWIND / UPDATE of a counter whose limits the run does not state

A scenario can plan ENQBUSY (RESP 55) for an ENQ by the RESOURCE operand as the program writes it; RESP2 is 0 because IBM states none for ENQBUSY. The ENQ must say NOSUSPEND: without it IBM suspends the task and the runtimes refuse. ENQ's other conditions come from the program's own operands, never from a plan: LENGTH outside 1 through 255 is LENGERR RESP2 1 and a MAXLIFETIME that is neither UOW nor TASK is INVREQ RESP2 2 (both modelled, as IBM states them). Refused: ENQBUSY planned for any other command, any other condition planned for ENQ, a RESP2 on an ENQBUSY plan, a planned-busy ENQ without NOSUSPEND, a resource that is no data-name of 1 to 16 characters, both bad operands at once (IBM names no order)

EXEC CICS HANDLE ABEND PROGRAM(name) names a program that gets control when the task abends. The det translator honours LABEL, CANCEL and RESET and refuses PROGRAM by name with this entry; the cobol-stub refuses it too (equivalence_cics.Unsupported), so the two sides agree

levels.condition: the program is in the estate's survey
levels.name: inventoried

levels.condition: the det translator leaves no hole and does not refuse it
levels.name: translated whole

levels.condition: a case runs it and the case's det port is equal on every scenario (CI's det-sweep ratchet on main; a Db2 case by a local sweep or the scheduled Db2 sweep's coverage ledger entry); the case's evidence record is reported, not required
levels.name: executed equivalent

levels.condition: L2, and the scenarios execute >= 100.0 percent of its live paragraphs
levels.name: paragraph coverage

levels.condition: L3, and >= 100.0 percent of its branch outcomes, net of the case's reviewed infeasible outcomes (listed under its assumptions)
levels.name: branch coverage

levels.condition: L4, and every surviving mutant of the det port's seeded mutation sample accounted for (stated equivalent / unreachable, owner-reviewed; a fresh det_mutation/ entry, #4628: the case, corpus and survivors list unchanged and the det port's bytes not found moved; generator, harness and oracle drift is recorded, not staling, #5862)
levels.name: mutants accounted for

mutation: det_mutation.py (#4628): a fresh entry, every survivor of the seeded sample accounted for

not_measured.what: data migration: VSAM / Db2 / sequential data converted and reconciled
the batch job streams that run the programs (steps, utilities, restart)
the estate's external interfaces (MQ, files exchanged, web services, other systems)
RACF / CICS security, user and transaction authorisation
the switch-over plan: parallel run, fallback, data freeze

oracle.what: GnuCOBOL plus the gitgalaxy CICS stub and models (CICS, Db2 precompiler, Language Environment, DISPLAY), not IBM z/OS

infeasible_stated.reason: `IF ETTL-RESP EQUAL DFHRESP(NORMAL) OR ETTL-STATUS EQUAL DFHVALUE(ENABLED)` (718) in 1310-TTL sits inside `IF ZF-TTL GREATER THAN SEVEN-DAYS` (716, 604800 s). ZF-TTL exceeds seven days only if it also exceeds twenty-four hours (86400 s), and then the test at 712-715 ran first: when ETTL-RESP is not NORMAL (or ETTL-STATUS is DISABLED) it MOVEs TWENTY-FOUR-HOURS to ZF-TTL, so 716 is false. Line 718 is therefore reached only with ETTL-RESP NORMAL, and its first operand ETTL-RESP EQUAL NORMAL is then true; no input makes both operands false.

undefined_by_ibm_stated.reason: `IF TTL-SECONDS NUMERIC` (704) is false only when the UNSTRING (699-702) puts a non-digit into `TTL-SECONDS` (PIC 9(06), USAGE DISPLAY), e.g. the query `ttl=abc`. The piece is an alphanumeric sender of a numeric MOVE: GnuCOBOL stores `000000`, so NUMERIC is true and 704:false is never taken; on z/OS the non-digit bytes stay and NUMERIC would be false. IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric DISPLAY item (Enterprise COBOL 6.4 Programming Guide SC27-8714-03, ZONEDATA(PFD) assumes valid data; register C11), so the outcome is undefined by IBM, not infeasible: an input does reach it. Scenario `post-ttl-nonnumeric` proves cobc's bytes, not z/OS's. Owner ruling 2026-10-31 (#6839 row J) extends family U from out-of-range subscripts and reference modifications (2026-10-29) to non-digit data in a numeric DISPLAY item.
